extracted.intended_audience: general learners and creative writers (poetry students / general audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and recognizing strong metaphors in poetry and prose: principles for what makes a good metaphor plus practical exercises to develop an ear and habit for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link two seemingly unrelated things to enliven scene or emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Metaphor brings a scene or emotion to life by linking two seemingly unrelated things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The metaphor functions by joining disparate elements so the comparison animates the scene or feeling; use this linking to make images vivid and immediate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reveal an unexpected resemblance and deepen perception
rubrics_metrics.description: A good metaphor reveals an unexpected resemblance and deepens perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for an element of surprise in the comparison that causes the reader to see the subject in a new, deeper way rather than stating the obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface meaning that direct statement cannot (read between the lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metaphor is a tool for 'reading between the lines' — surfacing meaning that direct statement cannot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use metaphor to suggest layers of meaning, implication, or feeling that straightforward description would flatten; rely on suggestion rather than explicit explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn from master exemplars
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples drawn from Langston Hughes and Carl Sandburg — masters of evocative metaphor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study poems and lines by accomplished practitioners to see how powerful metaphors are shaped and deployed; analyze what makes their comparisons effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and examine metaphors in everyday language and media
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice metaphors in everyday content (web blogs, newspapers, magazines) and examine ordinary expressions that are metaphors and similes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop the habit of spotting figurative language across common media and everyday speech; dissect these instances to understand how they work and which aspects are effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harvest metaphors from poetry collections and train your ear
rubrics_metrics.description: Search poetry collections to find metaphors; tune ear and mind to hear them in everyday speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly read poetry and practice active listening/attention to build a repertoire of images and an instinct for fresh comparisons; make deliberate exercises of seeking metaphors.
